anti_overlap: Do NOT audit the absent/empty/malformed field trichotomy or the additive-only fail-closed rule — that is fd-recall-failclosed's territory; you own only whether a PRESENT box lands on the right pixels.

Do NOT audit cross-language schema/serialization drift (key names, canonical bytes, conformance vectors) — that is fd-contract-drift's territory; assume the box decodes to the right integers and reason about the geometry from there.
Stay out of Swift actor/init-order/concurrency correctness except where a race changes WHICH frame_index a box is stamped with (geometry-relevant).
decision_lens: A geometry defect is P0/P1 only if it can move, shrink, or drop a box such that real face pixels end up OUTSIDE the redaction coverage that ships. A flip or scale error that makes the box LARGER or merely mislocated-but-still-covering is lower severity; one that undersizes/mislocates so a face survives unredacted is release-blocking. Rank strictly by residual unredacted-face risk, not by mathematical elegance.
focus: Coordinate-space correctness of the Apple Vision capture-face box as it travels device -> manifest -> node redaction coverage: the bottom-left -> top-left Y flip, the normalized[0,1] x1000 -> node-pixel scaling, letterbox/aspect-ratio composition, quantization, and degenerate-box hygiene.
name: fd-vision-geometry
persona: Apply the perspective of a computer-vision engineer who has shipped on-device face-detection pipelines across Apple Vision (VNDetectFaceRectangles, normalized bottom-left origin, EXIF-orientation-sensitive), CoreGraphics/CoreVideo coordinate spaces, and downstream letterboxed-inference resize math. This reviewer has been burned before by silent axis flips, off-by-one quantization at frame edges, non-square-pixel aspect-ratio distortion, and boxes that shift by exactly the padding of a letterbox nobody accounted for. They reason in pixels and normalized fractions simultaneously and always trace a single concrete face box end to end.
review_areas: The Y-axis flip in CaptureFaceDetector.convert: Vision boundingBox is bottom-left origin, contract is top-left; verify y1=1-origin.y-height and y2=1-origin.y are correct AND that VNImageRequestHandler orientation (default .up) matches the captured pixel-buffer orientation actually delivered by AVCaptureVideoDataOutput on a chest-mounted phone (portrait/landscape/mirrored front camera) — a wrong orientation silently rotates every box off the face.

The normalized->pixel scale in capture_face_detections: boxes are scaled to working_w x working_h (the LETTERBOXED working frame), then scale_boxes applies full_w/working_w. Verify this composition is correct when capture aspect ratio != node normalized-frame aspect ratio, and that no letterbox padding offset is being ignored (cascade boxes come back via map_box_from_letterbox already in working-frame coords; capture boxes bypass that path).

Quantize/clamp at frame edges: quantize() clamps to [0,1000] and Vision can return values slightly outside [0,1]; check that an edge-touching face box isn't clipped inward enough to expose a strip of face, and that floor-mins/ceil-maxs on the node side preserve outer extent.

Degenerate-box skip parity: Swift convert() skips x2<=x1 or y2<=y1; node _is_degenerate skips after scaling to a small frame. Verify a box that is valid at capture resolution but collapses to <1px at node working resolution is dropped SAFELY (it covered no real pixels) and cannot silently drop a box that still bounds visible face pixels.
conf_x100 rounding/clamp and whether confidence gating anywhere downstream (vision_face_conf_x100 tuple knob) could filter out a genuine capture-face box before it reaches coverage.

Whether the frame_index basis (per-segment passthrough counter, reset at rollover) actually aligns the box to the SAME decoded frame the node redacts — a box on the right geometry but the wrong frame is a full miss for that face.
severity_examples: P0: the Vision orientation passed to VNImageRequestHandler does not match the real capture pixel-buffer orientation, so every capture-face box is rotated/flipped off the actual face — the entire third recall path covers empty regions while faces go unredacted, and it passes CI because the synthetic wiring test never exercises real orientation.

P1: capture boxes are scaled to working_w x working_h assuming square-pixel proportional resize, but when capture AR differs from node-frame AR the normalized coords land on a stretched/letterboxed frame and the box is offset by the padding, shrinking coverage enough to expose part of a face.

P2: edge-touching face box has origin.x slightly negative from Vision; quantize clamps to 0 correctly, but the ceil/floor asymmetry combined with dilation=0 in a test-like config leaves a 1-2px sliver at the frame boundary uncovered.
success_hints: Trace ONE concrete face box (e.g. a face at the right edge of a portrait-orientation frame) numerically from VNFaceObservation.boundingBox through convert() -> manifest ints -> capture_face_detections() -> scale_boxes() -> destroy slice, and confirm the shipped redaction covers the original face pixels.

Compare the capture-box scaling path against how cascade boxes reach the same working space via letterbox_params/map_box_from_letterbox; if they land in different coordinate spaces before scale_boxes, that is the bug.

Check the real AVCaptureVideoDataOutput orientation contract on this app's capture path (portrait chest-mount, possibly front camera mirroring) against the hardcoded orientation: .up default and whether callers ever pass the real one.
Distinguish 'box is larger/mislocated but still covers the face' (low severity) from 'box undersized/shifted so face pixels leak' (release-blocking) for every geometry finding.
task_context: Find any path where the on-device capture-face pass lets a face go unredacted, where the coordinate flip (Vision bottom-left -> contract top-left x1000) or the normalized->pixel scaling in capture_face_detections mishandles a box, or where the fail-closed absence rule can be tricked into treating a missing/empty field as a clean 'no faces'. Verify the cross-language manifest contract (Swift writer <-> schema <-> node reader) can't drift. Rank by §8.5 redaction-recall risk. Your lens: the coordinate/geometry chain specifically — the Y flip, the normalized->pixel scale, letterbox/aspect-ratio composition, quantization at edges, and degenerate-box handling. A box on correct geometry but wrong frame, or wrong orientation, is a full face miss.
